purpose: Hands-on engineering manager and small-team head of engineering roles, especially AI-enabled product teams: hiring, team development, delivery improvement, technical ownership, and production operations while retaining direct implementation evidence.
scopeDecisions: Lead with hiring, the first in-house team, and delivery improvement; retain direct LLM architecture and classifier implementation before production and technical-debt evidence.
Keep the original Head of Product executive scope. Do not replace CEO reporting, team development, or investor communication with a generic hands-on summary.
Specify up to six people across engineering and design, not six engineers. The earlier RadiusAI team is a five-person data-collection lab, not an engineering department.

Keep the mixed-employer team-building group from the agreed selection, with explicit attribution at every source-role switch. Repeat attribution at a new group so production work is not assigned to the wrong Pause role.
Keep HPT-06 technical-debt remediation and HPT-08 CI/CD ownership. Workflow tooling remains reserve material rather than displacing those stronger management contributions.
The summary describes actual small-team leadership; it does not imply management of managers, a large department, or later hands-on model-training work.
skillEvidence: Hiring, engineer development/coaching, delivery, stakeholder management, and requirements practices come from the master competencies, role scope, and skills.
Python/Django and LLM architecture are anchored in the founding-role implementation bullets. Flutter, AWS, Azure, and API ownership are supported by the technical-direction source bullet.
CI/CD, production operations, and Sentry are explicit Head of Product work. Keep technical tools in support of leadership rather than turning this into a forecasting or computer-vision skills list.

contextReview.reason: Employer/title attribution identifies the company; team size includes design, and hiring responsibilities are concrete.
The preceding bullet introduces the in-house team. Clear cadence comparison and cost context support delivery leadership without inventing a cost metric.

At the employer switch, “the system’s initial training dataset” has no antecedent. Name the computer-vision assisted-checkout system the lab supported; retain lab operations and its five-person team as the leadership point.

The summary positions a hands-on leader but does not identify the specific platform. “The product” needs a short platform description when this separate hands-on group begins; preserve direct architecture evidence.
Self-contained domain, clinical validation, and implementation evidence. Good counterweight to management claims; rules/statistical-model qualification stays intact.
This new production group introduces an unnamed inherited system. Clarify that platform scope so the reader can distinguish stabilization from the preceding LLM feature work.
AWS/Django is established in the earlier architecture bullet; role attribution identifies the later leadership work. Delivery alongside remediation is explicit and relevant.
Concrete production ownership and incident work support player-coach roles. Continues the explicitly attributed Head of Product role; no external system referent is required.
